name: VIPer22A
full_name: Low Power Off-Line SMPS Primary Switcher
description: Monolithic off-line switched-mode power supply primary switcher combining a fixed-frequency (60kHz) current-mode PWM controller with a 730V-rated power MOSFET on the same die. Drives a flyback (or buck) transformer directly from rectified mains with no separate startup circuit: a high-voltage current source built into the DRAIN pin charges the VDD capacitor at power-on, then hands off to the auxiliary winding once VDD reaches VDDon. Includes auto-restart (hiccup mode) protection against overtemperature, overcurrent, and VDD overvoltage. Higher-current sibling of the VIPER12A in the low-power VIPER family, with a lower-rDS(on) internal MOSFET giving roughly 1.5x the typical power capability at the same package.

typical_application: Low-power off-line flyback SMPS at slightly higher output power than the VIPER12A: battery-charger adapters, standby power supplies for TVs/monitors, and auxiliary supplies for motor control, where a fully integrated PWM controller plus 730V MOSFET removes the need for a separate startup circuit and MOSFET. The wide VDD input range accommodates auxiliary-winding voltage swings well, and automatic burst mode reduces standby/no-load power.
gotchas: DRAIN doubles as the high-voltage startup current source: before the auxiliary winding takes over, DRAIN charges the external VDD capacitor directly through an internal HV current source -- do not assume VDD is only ever fed from the transformer's aux winding

FB is a current-mode control input with a useful range of only 0V to 1V; shorting FB to SOURCE forces maximum peak drain current (used deliberately for current-limit testing, not a safe default wiring)

VDD has hysteretic on/off thresholds (typ 14.5V on, 8V off) -- if the auxiliary supply's minimum voltage sags below VDDoff under load, the part will restart in HICCUP mode rather than latch off cleanly

rDS(on) rises sharply with junction temperature (15-17 ohm typ at 25C vs 31 ohm max at 100C) -- thermal design at rated power must use the 100C figure, not the room-temperature datasheet headline number
SO-8 and DIP-8 share the same pin function order but not the same power rating: DIP-8's larger lead frame roughly doubles typical power capability over SO-8 for the same part number

overtemperature, overcurrent, and VDD overvoltage faults all trigger the same auto-restart HICCUP behavior rather than a latched shutdown -- design assuming the converter will keep retrying at DRST (~16% duty cycle) under a persistent fault, not stop

not pin-for-pin interchangeable in rating with VIPER12A despite the identical pinout and package options -- the lower rDS(on) gives VIPER22A roughly 1.5x the typical power capability; do not assume the two are drop-in equivalents for a design pushed near VIPER12A's limit
